title: How to update cursor in Cursor on Mac: a step by step guide for developers

description: Learn how to update Cursor on Mac using the built-in menu, command palette, or manual installation to ensure you have the latest AI coding features.
intro: To update Cursor on your Mac, click Cursor in the menu bar and select Check for Updates. You can also trigger an update manually by using the Command Palette with the shortcut ⌘ ⇧ P and searching for the update command.
tldr: Use the Cursor menu bar option to check for new versions.
Open the Command Palette with ⌘ ⇧ P to force an update check.
Download the latest DMG from the official website if in-app updates fail.
Check your current version in the About Cursor menu.

blocks.text: The most reliable way to check for updates is through the standard macOS menu bar. Cursor follows the traditional Mac app structure. When you have the application open, look at the top of your screen. You will see the word Cursor in the menu bar next to the Apple icon. Click this to reveal the application menu.

Inside this menu, look for the option labeled Check for Updates. If a new version is available, a small window will appear. It will show you the version number and a summary of changes. Click the Install button to begin the download. Once the files are ready, the app will prompt you to restart. This applies the updates and brings your editor to the latest state.

If you prefer to keep your hands on the keyboard, the Command Palette is your best tool. It is the central hub for almost every action in the editor. Press ⌘ ⇧ P to bring up the search bar at the top of the window. Start typing the word update. You should see a command that says Attempt Update or Check for Updates.

Select this command by pressing Enter. The editor will perform a silent check in the background. If an update is found, it will notify you immediately. This method is faster than clicking through menus, especially if you are already in the middle of a coding session. It avoids the need to move your mouse away from your code.

Sometimes the automatic update mechanism may fail due to network restrictions or file permission issues. In these cases, a manual update is the most effective solution. Visit the official Cursor website and download the latest DMG file. You do not need to uninstall the old version first. Just open the downloaded file and drag the Cursor application into your Applications folder.

The system will ask if you want to replace the existing file. Confirm this action. Your settings, extensions, and AI configurations are stored in a separate directory. They will remain intact after the update. This process ensures that all binary files are fresh and correctly placed on your Mac.

It is helpful to know which version you are running. Go to Cursor > About Cursor in the menu bar. This window displays your current build number and the version of the underlying VS Code engine. Developers often check this when troubleshooting issues with specific AI models or plugins. If you notice strange behavior, checking your version against the latest changelog is a good first step.

Cursor updates its AI models and features frequently. Sometimes these updates are rolled out in stages. If you do not see an update, you might be in a cohort that has not received the rollout yet. Wait a few days, and the update will likely appear in your menu. Always check the official changelog for details on what has changed in the latest build.

faq.question: How often does Cursor update?
faq.answer: Cursor releases updates frequently, often on a weekly basis, to introduce new AI features and model improvements.

faq.question: Will I lose my settings when I update?
faq.answer: No, your settings and extensions are stored in your user directory and will persist through the update process.

faq.question: What if the update fails?
faq.answer: If the in-app update fails, download the latest version directly from the official website and overwrite your existing installation.
